title: Are your AI habits safe?
description: A few everyday decisions about information, permissions, and sharing.

questions.question: Which information should never be pasted into an ordinary AI prompt?
questions.explanation: Access tokens and passwords are credentials. Keep them out of prompts, logs, and shared documents.

questions.question: Is removing names always enough to anonymize a document?
options: Yes, names are the only identifiers
No, other details can still identify someone
Yes, if it is a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Dates, locations, roles, and combinations of details can still identify people.

questions.question: What should you check before uploading workplace data?
options: Whether the tool has a bright logo
Only whether the tool is free
Organizational approval, data requirements, and the product’s controls
questions.explanation: Approval and suitable data controls matter regardless of price or popularity.

questions.question: A shared AI conversation link may expose what?
options: The information included in the shared conversation
Nothing, because it is an AI product
Only the title, in every product
questions.explanation: Sharing behavior varies. Review exactly what a link exposes and who can access it.

questions.question: You accidentally share a credential. What is the better response?
options: Delete the chat and assume the problem is solved
Follow the incident process and rotate the credential
Wait for the next password reminder
questions.explanation: A credential may remain compromised after a message is deleted. Follow the relevant response process and replace it.

questions.question: What is a safer way to learn a customer-data workflow?
options: Upload the largest real dataset first
Use fictional records in a small test
Post the records publicly for feedback
questions.explanation: Synthetic records let you test the process without exposing real customer information.
